entries.claim: nba2k17-ws.2ksports.com is a historical NBA 2K17 web-service hostname.
entries.notes: The 2023 replacement-service developer report is independently corroborated by a 2018-era game HOSTS list that labels nba2k17-ws.2ksports.com under NBA 2K17. This strongly supports the hostname, but not exact routes or ports.

entries.claim: Port 17217 was used by a historical public NBA 2K17 private-server implementation.
entries.notes: Establishes historical significance of the port, not the complete retail-client contract.

entries.claim: A 2023 NBA 2K17 PC replacement-service developer reported success using a locally trusted certificate path.
entries.notes: Does not prove absence of certificate pinning for every client build.

entries.claim: sanitized-fixtures/probe.66686d164ca1.sanitized.jsonl contains lab self-test traffic, not NBA 2K17 client traffic.
entries.notes: May validate instrument behavior only; must never promote TLS/HTTP values from this file to OBSERVED_2K17.

entries.claim: Granite exposes a 16-byte big-endian field-record framing with a zero terminator and data section for NBA 2K19.
entries.notes: This is not evidence that NBA 2K17 uses the same framing.

entries.claim: A Plutonium administrator reported that their prior NBA 2K17 investigation found an HTTP API for most live-service tasks with custom/binary body serialization.
entries.notes: Supports existence of an HTTP API and some binary/custom serialization, but not exact framing, routes, field IDs or VcFieldList compatibility.

entries.claim: A Plutonium administrator reported that the NBA 2K17 backend expected a special HTTPS client certificate.
entries.notes: The second source independently shows an NBA 2K17 server-emulator researcher believed mTLS/client-certificate auth was in use. Exact certificate format, key location, route coverage and universal requirement remain unverified.

entries.claim: A Plutonium administrator reported that NBA 2K17 game traffic used a combination of WebSockets and UDP, with WebSockets appearing to serve neighborhood/Park behavior and UDP the actual match.
entries.notes: This is a specific prior-investigation report, not a packet capture. Exact WebSocket endpoint, handshake, UDP ports and packet formats remain unknown.

entries.claim: A Plutonium administrator reported that NBA 2K17 caches some files obtained from its HTTP API on disk.
entries.notes: The source suggests updated player lists/small patches as examples but does not publish filenames, hashes or cache paths.

entries.claim: Revival's first-party status page separates its NBA 2K17 replacement infrastructure into Revival API, game servers handling login/matchmaking/game wire, and Park servers.
entries.notes: This is evidence about Revival's replacement architecture, not proof that the original 2K17 production backend used the same topology.

entries.claim: Revival publicly reported a live NBA 2K17 beta with playable MyCareer in July 2026 and currently lists Play Now Online, MyCourt and MyPARK as service modes.
entries.notes: Strong evidence of replacement-service feasibility and feature coverage, but no wire-schema details.

entries.claim: Preserve's first-party NBA 2K17 page lists an available 69.2 GB package labeled version 1.0.1; the public Preserve client documents SHA-256 verification for downloaded files.
entries.notes: Package version labeling does not establish a specific NBA2K17.exe file version, Steam build ID or executable hash.

entries.claim: Contemporary NBA 2K17 PC reports place SYNC.BIN under Steam/userdata/<user>/385760/local and say it is created or written near startup before the main menus.
entries.notes: One user estimated the resulting file at roughly 900 MB. Treat that size as anecdotal, not canonical.

entries.claim: A contemporary NBA 2K17 Steam support thread reports that removing the 385760 remote data caused the game to report corruption and redownload files from 2K servers, after which the affected modes worked again.
entries.notes: Supports server-backed restore/sync behavior in the user-data area. It does not identify the exact transport or which files were fetched by the HTTP API versus other services.

entries.claim: Historical NBA 2K17 modding documentation distinguishes SYNC.BIN in the local directory from roster files such as Roster0001 and RosterDescriptions in remote, and describes official roster/update data as normally downloaded by legitimate copies from game servers.
entries.notes: Useful for cache-file roles and layout. Third-party redistributed files are not accepted as canonical original byte content.

entries.claim: Historical 2K17 modding pages report that SYNC.BIN affects default/content data and may need to be edited for some court/content mods; the NLSC 2K17 archive also lists a 2016 tutorial specifically about preventing 2K SYNC.BIN updates.
entries.notes: Supports SYNC.BIN as a server-updated/default-content artifact candidate. Internal container format remains unknown.
